newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to off, pork bellies lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to off, pork bellies lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb lower while pork bellies were called 0.200 to 0.400 cent a lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Mostly steady to lower cash hog indications and further weakness in cash pork products were expected to prompt carryover selling interest in hog futures. Futures set 2-1/2-week lows Monday and reflected cash weakness, sources said. Packer demand recently has been tempered because their cutout margins are still unprofitable, analysts said.
USDA quoted pork cut-out values fell another $0.46 to $0.54 per cwt on Monday.

High pork prices in April cut off domestic and foreign demand for pork, but analysts noted that some interest is starting to develop for pork at the lower levels which may spark support in futures soon. Cash markets may be reaching a bottom, they added.
Renewed selling was seen in pork belly futures after losses were pared late Monday. The weak tone to cash bellies were expected to keep futures pressured, analysts said.
Cash belly prices declined another $3 to $5 per cwt Monday with 14-16 lb bellies trading down to $78 to $80, $10 to $12 down from the recent high.
Delivery concerns will likely remain in May with 115 deliveries posted on the first day and partly through April 30, they said.
However, some analysts are looking for futures and cash to bottom soon.
Interest will develop for product at the lower prices and as continued light slaughter reduces offerings. Storings are also non-existent, they added.

Estimates on Tuesday afternoon's weekly CME out-of-town storage report ranged from unchanged to out 200,000 lbs. This compares with an out-movement of 1.205 million lbs last week and an in-movement of 333,000 lbs last year.
